page: Hetzner Cloud ccx63 is a dedicated CPU server instance built on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 48 vCPUs derived from 24 physical AMD EPYC cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system is provisioned with 188.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.91 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided locally via a 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the virtualization layer is managed by QEMU. No public IPv4 addresses are included by default, and there are no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core and cryptographic performance. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 73209.23 and a PassMark CPU score of 64305.59, both placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Cryptographic capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA-NI instruction sets, resulting in a strong PassMark CPU encryption score of 58566.64. Memory bandwidth remains moderate, with uncached read and write speeds of 148.56 GB/sec and 80.13 GB/sec respectively. In database-oriented tasks, the server demonstrated high throughput, executing 62.09 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring 22243.57 in PassMark database operations.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-core ratio, the ccx63 is suited for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, and database hosting. Software compilation benchmarks using Clang scored in the top 25%, making it viable for CI/CD pipelines. Additionally, the server exhibits strong performance in small-model LLM text generation, reaching 360.33 tokens per second. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores offer reliable resource density and predictable performance without the CPU stealing risks associated with shared-core instances, representing a balanced cost-to-performance profile for compute-heavy and database workloads.
